problem_definition: Optical biosensor calibration drift due to LED aging
baseline_architecture: The biosensor uses a primary LED to emit light for optical biosensing, but its calibration drifts over time due to LED aging.
inventive_nucleus: A thermally conductive polymer encapsulates the primary LED to reduce thermal stress and slow down aging, while utilizing a temperature-compensated thermal interface to maintain optimal thermal conductivity across various temperature conditions, and incorporating a phase-change material to enhance thermal conductivity under extreme temperatures.
mechanism: The polymer encapsulation interacts with the primary LED through thermal conduction, reducing thermal stress and slowing down aging.
causal_chain: Optical biosensor calibration drift due to LED aging
Thermally conductive polymer reduces thermal stress
Phase-change material enhances thermal conductivity under extreme temperatures
Reduced thermal stress slows down LED aging
Slower LED aging minimizes calibration drift
Stable calibration baseline maintained over time
system_architecture: The phase-change material is integrated into the existing biosensor design, surrounding the primary LED and secondary reference LED.
operating_conditions: The system operates under normal temperature conditions (20-40°C).
boundary_conditions: The polymer encapsulation contains the failure by reducing the primary LED's aging rate, thereby minimizing the need for real-time normalization.
expected_effect: The system maintains a stable optical signal baseline over time.
